# A quaternion-lift argument for the Barnes–Wall orbifold anomaly

**26 November 2026 — Proposed proof; exact finite calculations reproduced internally; external expert review pending.** This text and the accompanying code were generated by coordinated AI agents. Separate agents performed the internal mathematical reviews and two different implementations of the lift calculation. No external expert has verified the argument, and no priority claim is made.

## Abstract and attribution

Keller, Ashley Winter Roberts and Jeremy Roberts constructed a holomorphic orbifold of the rank-128 Barnes–Wall lattice VOA conditional on the vanishing of an extraspecial-group anomaly [KRR, Conjecture 5.2]. We give a candidate argument for that vanishing. A compatible lift of a specific generalized quaternion group of order 16 removes the residual anomaly that cyclic tests alone cannot detect. We also give a direct proof that all involutions in the prescribed extraspecial action are standard lifts. A block argument proves the compatibility of the quaternion lift analytically. Exact finite calculations corroborate this argument and the source phase formulas; a separate implementation reconstructs them by a different method. Two simple-current extensions and an explicit positivity lemma equip the resulting full orbifold with a unitary structure. A global discrete-torsion average gives a member with at most $5\,057\,652$ weight-four states. The anomaly argument extends to every odd parameter $m\ge5$, with a genuine obstruction at $m=3$; the resulting family has exact primary gap four for odd $m\ge7$ and an exact weight-four count for odd $m\ge9$.

The Barnes–Wall action, proposed orbifold, twisted-module calculations and spectral analysis are due to KRR. The contribution proposed here is the compatible quaternion lift and its use with established group cohomology, together with the standardness, unitarity, discrete-torsion bound and uniform-family arguments below. The resulting proposed construction is a unitary strongly rational holomorphic VOA of central charge 128 with primary gap four. It does not concern the existence of an extremal VOA at central charge 48.

## 1. Statement and conventions

Let $L=BW(7)$, with exactly the ordered lattice basis of [KRR, (A.1.1)]. Let
$$
E=2^{1+14}_+
$$
act on $V_L$ through the sign lifts of [KRR, (2.2.1)–(2.2.4), Theorem 3.5]. Write $z=-I$ for its central involution, $A=E/\langle z\rangle\cong\mathbb F_2^{14}$, and $\pi:E\to A$. The quadratic form associated with this central extension is
$$
Q(s,t)=\sum_{i=1}^{7}s_it_i.
$$
Thus a lift of $a\in A$ has square $z^{Q(a)}$. We identify $H^3(G,U(1))$ with $H^4(G,\mathbb Z)$ for a finite group $G$.

**Proposed theorem.** The anomaly $\alpha\in H^3(E,U(1))$ of the specified action on $V_{BW(7)}$ is zero.

The theorem is about this particular action, including its lattice-VOA phases. Lattice isometries without their compatible lifts would not suffice. Sections 6–7 give the unitary full-orbifold consequence. Section 8 bounds its lightest-state multiplicity for some coherent discrete-torsion choice. Section 9 states and proves the extension to the family $E_m=2_+^{1+2m}$.

All matrices below act on row lattice coordinates from the right. Products of lifts are read in the corresponding order. The quotient quadratic form $Q$, the conformal weight $\rho$, and the quadratic sign exponents $q_R$ are different objects.

## 2. A cohomological detection lemma

We use the extraspecial-group computation of [JFT, §3.3]. At width seven it gives
$$
H^4(E,\mathbb Z)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^{454}\oplus\mathbb Z/4.
\tag{1}
$$
The image $X$ of inflation from $H^4(A,\mathbb Z)$ is elementary abelian of dimension 455, hence is exactly the 2-torsion subgroup. These dimensions follow directly from the filtration in that section: $H^4(A,\mathbb Z)$ has dimension $14+\binom{14}{2}+\binom{14}{3}=469$, and the inflation kernel has dimension 14. This uses the corrected rank obtained from the filtration, rather than the typographical rank formula noted in [KRR, §5.3].

### 2.1 The distinguished quadratic class

Let $x_i\in H^1(A,\mathbb F_2)$ be coordinates and $\beta$ the integral Bockstein. Put
$$
q=Q(\beta x_1,\ldots,\beta x_{14})\in H^4(A,\mathbb Z),
\qquad \widetilde q=\pi^*q.
$$
Here the variables in the quadratic polynomial are integral classes of degree two. Reduction modulo two sends $q$ to $Q(x)^2$. Since $Q$ is the extension class, $\pi^*Q=0$ in mod-2 cohomology. Consequently $\widetilde q$ has zero mod-2 reduction and is divisible by two in $H^4(E,\mathbb Z)$.

Choose a quaternion subgroup $H\cong Q_8$ whose image in $A$ is an anisotropic plane: its basis $a,b$ satisfies $Q(a)=Q(b)=1$ and $B_Q(a,b)=1$. The bilinear condition is essential. On that plane the extension form is
$$
Q_H(x,y)=x^2+xy+y^2.
$$
Write $X=\beta x$, $Y=\beta y$. The integral Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre differential used in [JFT, §3.3] is $d_3(\ell)=\beta(\ell Q_H)$. Its reductions give $d_3(x)=X^2$ and $d_3(y)=Y^2$. Thus the inflation image in total degree four is the nonzero one-dimensional quotient spanned by $XY$; no later differential enters bidegree $(4,0)$. Therefore
$$
\widetilde q|_H=\operatorname{Inf}(X^2+XY+Y^2)
              =\operatorname{Inf}(XY)\ne0.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular $\widetilde q$ is the unique nonzero element divisible by two in (1). This supplies the quaternion-detection fact directly, without relying on wording that omits the anisotropic-plane condition.

### 2.2 Cyclic restrictions and Boolean cubics

Put $U_i=\beta x_i$. An explicit integral basis for $H^4(A,\mathbb Z)$, compatible with [JFT, §3.1], is
$$
U_i^2,\qquad U_iU_j\ (i<j),\qquad
\beta(x_ix_jx_k)\ (i<j<k).
$$
On the line generated by $a$, these restrict respectively to $a_i$, $a_ia_j$, and $a_ia_ja_k$, times the generator of $H^4(C_2,\mathbb Z)$. For the third family, if $t$ generates $H^1(C_2,\mathbb F_2)$, then $\beta(t^3)$ generates $H^4(C_2,\mathbb Z)$. The resulting degree-one, degree-two and degree-three squarefree monomials are linearly independent as Boolean functions, and their number is 469. This gives an identification with squarefree Boolean polynomials of degree at most three and zero constant term, under which cyclic restriction is evaluation. The explicit type-I, type-II and type-III cocycles in [Yu, (6)] give the same description.

We need the following elementary lemma, stated only at the dimension needed here.

**Boolean lemma.** If a squarefree polynomial $f(u,v)$ of degree at most three on $\mathbb F_2^7\oplus\mathbb F_2^7$ vanishes on every point with $\sum u_iv_i=0$, then
$$
f=Q\left(\delta+\sum_i\beta_i u_i+\sum_i\gamma_i v_i\right)
\tag{3}
$$
in the Boolean ring, where each coordinate satisfies $x^2=x$.

**Proof.** The restrictions $f(u,0)$ and $f(0,v)$ vanish, so uniqueness of squarefree polynomial representation removes all terms using just one block of variables. Evaluating $u=e_i$ with arbitrary $v_i=0$, and then $v=e_i$ with arbitrary $u_i=0$, leaves only
$$
f=\sum_i u_iv_i\left(A_i+\sum_{j\ne i}B_{ij}u_j+\sum_{j\ne i}C_{ij}v_j\right).
$$
Set $u_i=v_i=u_k=v_k=1$ for distinct $i,k$, all other coordinates initially zero. The point is singular. Varying $u_j$ for $j\notin\{i,k\}$ gives $B_{ij}=B_{kj}$. Thus every off-diagonal column is constant, $B_{ij}=\beta_j$. Likewise $C_{ij}=\gamma_j$. At the original two-pair point,
$$
A_i+\beta_i+\gamma_i=A_k+\beta_k+\gamma_k.
$$
Call the common value $\delta$. Expanding (3) with $x^2=x$ gives the displayed expression. $\square$

The inflation-kernel differential in [JFT, §3.3] is $\ell\mapsto Sq^1(\ell Q)$. Under the preceding restriction description, these classes are the Boolean polynomials $\ell Q$: the integral Bockstein of the homogeneous cubic $\ell Q$ reduces to $Sq^1(\ell Q)$, and its cyclic restriction is $\ell(a)Q(a)$.

**Detection lemma.** A class $\eta\in H^4(E,\mathbb Z)$ is zero if it restricts to zero on every cyclic involution subgroup and on one quaternion subgroup with anisotropic quotient plane.

**Proof.** If $\eta$ had order four, then $2\eta=\widetilde q$, contradicting (2) and $\eta|_H=0$. Hence $\eta$ is 2-torsion and lies in the inflation image $X$. Write $\eta=\pi^*\nu$. Each nonzero singular vector of $A$ has an order-two lift, on which $\pi$ is an isomorphism. Therefore the Boolean polynomial for $\nu$ vanishes on $Q=0$. Equation (3) and the inflation-kernel description leave only $\eta=\delta\widetilde q$. Equation (2) then forces $\delta=0$. $\square$

## 3. Standardness of the prescribed involutions

This section proves the necessary cyclic condition directly. It does not use the assertion that every tensor word containing a $Y=XZ$ factor is fixed-point-free: for example, $Y_1Y_2$ is an involution with a 64-dimensional real fixed space. The proof below also covers these even-$Y$ tensor words.

Label the KRR lattice basis by subsets $I$ of seven tensor factors. Modulo two, its parity-zero space $V_0$ consists of odd-cardinality subsets and $V_1$ of even-cardinality subsets. From [KRR, (A.2.8)–(A.2.11)],
$$
X_i=I+A_i^+,\qquad Z_i=I+A_i^-,
$$
where $A_i^+$ adds factor $i$ to an odd subset when absent, $A_i^-$ removes it when present, and both kill $V_1$. Every product $A_i^\epsilon A_j^\eta$ is zero. Hence
$$
R=z^\epsilon\prod_iX_i^{s_i}Z_i^{t_i}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
R-I=N=\sum_i(s_iA_i^++t_iA_i^-)
\tag{4}
$$
over $\mathbb F_2$.

Put $W=\operatorname{span}(e_2,\ldots,e_7)$ and split
$$
V_0=\Lambda^{\rm odd}W\oplus e_1\wedge\Lambda^{\rm even}W.
$$
Write the $V_0$ component of a vector as $(x,y)$. On either parity subspace define the complementary-pair quadratic
$$
\mathfrak q(u)=\sum_{\{I,I^c\}}u_Iu_{I^c},
\tag{5}
$$
with each unordered complementary pair of subsets of the six factors counted once. Complementation preserves parity.

For the canonical sign lifts in KRR the phase exponents are
$$
q_{X_1}=\mathfrak q_{\rm odd}(x),\qquad
q_{Z_1}=\mathfrak q_{\rm even}(y),\qquad
q_{X_i}=q_{Z_i}=0\quad(i\ge2).
\tag{6}
$$
To see this directly, decompose the binary half-Gram matrix as $H=H_1+H_2$ using [KRR, Lemmas A.1–A.3]. The matrix $H_2$ is supported on $V_0\times V_0$, while $H_1(e_I)=e_{I^c}$ when $1\in I$ and is zero otherwise. Since $A$ maps $V_0$ to $V_1$ and kills $V_1$, $H_2$ contributes nothing to the defect
$$
H-(I+A)H(I+A)^T=AH+HA^T+AHA^T.
$$
For $A_1^+$, the surviving term $AH_1$ pairs first-factor-absent odd subsets with their complementary six-factor subsets. For $A_1^-$, the term $H_1A^T$ gives the corresponding first-factor-present pairs. Taking the strict lower triangle gives (6); for the other factors the defect terms cancel as in KRR Lemmas A.3–A.4. Each first-factor quadratic has exactly 16 monomials. Both checkers also verify (6) coefficient by coefficient from the full half-Gram matrix.

These phases depend only on $V_0$, whose coordinates are unchanged by every binary generator. Thus the prescribed product lift has phase
$$
q_R=s_1\mathfrak q_{\rm odd}(x)+t_1\mathfrak q_{\rm even}(y).
\tag{7}
$$

Let
$$
C=\sum_{i=2}^7(s_i e_i\wedge+t_i\iota_i),\qquad
Q_0=\sum_{i=2}^7s_it_i.
$$
The Clifford relations in characteristic two give $C^2=Q_0I$. The polar form of (5) is
$$
B(u,v)=[e_2\wedge\cdots\wedge e_7](u\wedge v).
$$
Wedge and contraction are self-adjoint for this pairing, so
$$
B(Cu,Cv)=Q_0B(u,v).
$$
The function $\mathfrak q(Cu)+Q_0\mathfrak q(u)$ is therefore linear. It vanishes on each coordinate vector $e_I$: the support of $Ce_I$ consists of subsets differing from $I$ in one bit, whereas complementary subsets differ in six bits. Hence
$$
\mathfrak q(Cu)=Q_0\mathfrak q(u).
\tag{8}
$$

For a binary fixed vector, (4) gives
$$
Cx+t_1y=0,\qquad s_1x+Cy=0.
\tag{9}
$$
An involution has $Q_0=s_1t_1$. If $(s_1,t_1)=(0,0)$, (7) is zero. If $(1,0)$, then $x=Cy$, and (8) gives $\mathfrak q(x)=0$. The case $(0,1)$ is analogous. If $(1,1)$, then $y=Cx$ and $\mathfrak q(y)=\mathfrak q(x)$, again making (7) zero.

The phase therefore vanishes on the entire binary fixed space. Every integral fixed vector reduces to that space, so all the prescribed involution lifts are standard. The central involution already has trivial phase.

The real eigenvalue multiplicities from [KRR, (3.2.2)–(3.2.5)] then give twisted ground-state weight 4 for a noncentral involution and 8 for the central involution. Their cyclic types $2^2\rho\bmod2$ are zero. This proves all involution restrictions required by the detection lemma.

For the orbifold consequence below, also note that every order-four element of $E$ squares to $-I$, so its lattice isometry is fixed-point-free and its prescribed lift is standard. Its twisted ground-state weight is 6 by [KRR, §3.2]. Thus every nontrivial $E$-twisted sector has ground weight at least four.

The optional finite confirmation enumerates all 8,256 singular quotient vectors: 2,080 have identically zero phase, and all 6,176 remaining phase forms vanish on the complete binary kernel. It checks 197,632 kernel-basis values and 3,063,296 polarization values, without integral-nullspace or floating-point assumptions.

## 4. The compatible quaternion lift

In Cartesian tensor coordinates put
$$
X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=XZ.
$$
Tensor positions are numbered $1,\ldots,7$ in KRR order: position $a$ is source bit $i[7-a]$. Define
$$
a=Y_1,\qquad b=Z_1Y_2,\qquad
g=\frac{(I+Y_1)(X_3+Z_3)}2.
\tag{10}
$$
The factors in $g$ commute. Since $Y_1^T=-Y_1$, $Y_1^2=-I$ and $(X_3+Z_3)^2=2I$, the matrix $g$ is orthogonal. Direct tensor multiplication gives
$$
g^2=a,\qquad a^2=b^2=g^4=z=-I,\qquad bgbg=z.
\tag{11}
$$
For the last relation, conjugation by $b$ negates $Y_1$ and fixes $X_3+Z_3$, giving $bgb^{-1}=g^{-1}$.

### 4.1 Integral rows and the lattice subgroup

Write $e_i$ for the ordered KRR lattice basis vector with seven-bit index $i$. Put $p_i=(7-|i|)\bmod2$, where $|i|$ counts one-bits, and let $i^S$ denote toggling the positions in $S$. The source rows [KRR, (A.2.5)–(A.2.6)] imply
$$
e_i(X_3+Z_3)=2^{p_i}e_{i^{\{3\}}},\qquad
e_iY_1=(-1)^{i_1}\bigl(e_i-2^{p_i}e_{i^{\{1\}}}\bigr).
$$
Toggling one bit exchanges $p_i$ and $1-p_i$. Substitution into (10) therefore gives
$$
e_ig=
\begin{cases}
2^{p_i}e_{i^{\{3\}}}-e_{i^{\{1,3\}}},&i_1=0,\\
e_{i^{\{1,3\}}},&i_1=1.
\end{cases}
$$
Thus $g$ has integral lattice coordinates. Equation (11) gives $g^8=I$, so its inverse is integral as well; hence $g\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$.

The matrix $g$ has order eight, and $b$ is not a power of $g$: it conjugates $g$ to $g^{-1}\ne g$. The relations consequently give $\langle g,b\rangle\cong Q_{16}$ of order sixteen, with $\langle a,b\rangle\cong Q_8$. The images of $a,b$ in $A$ satisfy $Q(a)=Q(b)=B_Q(a,b)=1$, so their plane is the required anisotropic plane.

### 4.2 A block lemma for canonical lifts

Let $G$ be the KRR Gram matrix and $H$ its lower half: the strictly lower entries are those of $G$, the diagonal is $G_{ii}/2$, and the upper entries are zero. The lattice cocycle is $\epsilon(v,w)=(-1)^{vHw^T}$. For a lattice isometry $R$, the canonical lift is
$$
B_R=\operatorname{strictlower}(H-RHR^T)\bmod2,
\qquad
\widehat R(e^v)=(-1)^{vB_Rv^T}e^{vR}.
\tag{12}
$$
The defect is symmetric modulo two with zero diagonal, and $B_R+B_R^T$ equals it; hence (12) is a valid cocycle lift. Its phase is zero on every lattice basis vector. We continue to read lift products in right-action order, consistently with row coordinates.

**Block lemma.** Suppose the lattice basis is partitioned into blocks on each of which $H$ restricts to zero modulo two. On the subgroup of lattice isometries preserving the span of each block, canonical lifts form a group homomorphism.

**Proof.** For such an isometry $R$, the rows indexed by one block are supported in that block. Thus both $H$ and $RHR^T$ vanish on the block modulo two, as does $B_R$. The phase $q_R(v)=vB_Rv^T$ consequently vanishes for every vector supported in a single block. For two such isometries $R,S$, the product lift has phase
$$
q_R(e_i)+q_S(e_iR)=0
$$
on every basis vector, just as the canonical lift of $RS$ does. Two lifts of the same lattice isometry differ on the lattice group algebra by a lattice character, as follows by dividing their cocycle-lift identities. A character trivial on the basis is trivial everywhere. Their Heisenberg actions also agree, proving equality of the VOA automorphisms. $\square$

To apply the lemma, let $d(i,j)$ be Hamming distance. The KRR basis (A.1.1) gives the exact Gram formula
$$
G_{ij}
=2^{\lceil(7-|i|)/2\rceil+\lceil(7-|j|)/2\rceil+|i\cap j|-4}
=2^{\,3-d(i,j)/2+(p_i+p_j)/2}.
$$
The exponent is integral, and $H_{ii}=2^{2+p_i}$ is even. Partition the basis according to its four bits in positions $4,5,6,7$. This gives sixteen blocks of eight vectors. Within a block, $d(i,j)\le3$, so the Gram exponent is at least two. Every within-block Gram entry is therefore divisible by four, and $H$ restricts to zero modulo two. No condition on pairings between distinct blocks is required.

The matrices $X_1,Z_1,X_2,Z_2$ preserve each block by their source row formulas. The row formula in §4.1 shows that $g$ does too. The block lemma thus applies to all matrices needed here.

### 4.3 Agreement with the prescribed action

Retain the prescribed products
$\widehat a=\widehat X_1\widehat Z_1$ and
$\widehat b=\widehat Z_1\widehat X_2\widehat Z_2$.
Their generator lifts are exactly the canonical lifts of KRR. The block lemma makes them the canonical lifts of $a,b$ and lifts every relation (11). In particular,
$$
\widehat g^{\,2}=\widehat a,\qquad
\widehat a^{\,2}=\widehat b^{\,2}=\widehat z,\qquad
\widehat b\widehat g\widehat b\widehat g=\widehat z.
\tag{13}
$$
No character correction is required. Since the canonical lift homomorphism projects to the original lattice action, it embeds this $Q_{16}$, gives $\widehat g$ actual order eight, and agrees with the prescribed $E$ action on the common $Q_8$.

The two accompanying exact implementations independently reproduce the lattice and phase identities as supplementary verification of this analytic argument. The argument itself requires no enumeration of 128-dimensional phase coefficients. It makes no assertion about lifting the whole Barnes–Wall normalizer.

## 5. Restriction through $Q_{16}$

The eigenvalues of $g$ are the primitive eighth roots with exponents $1,3,5,7$, each of multiplicity 32. The matrix is fixed-point-free, and (13) gives actual lift order eight. Its standard twisted ground-state weight is
$$
\rho_g=\frac{32}{4\cdot8^2}(7+15+15+7)=\frac{11}{2}.
$$
The cyclic type is $8^2\rho_g=352\equiv0\pmod8$. Therefore the anomaly of the $Q_{16}$ action restricts to zero on its $C_8$ subgroup.

For completeness, the needed quaternion-group restriction statement follows from the free $S^3$ action. A finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset SU(2)$ acts freely on $S^3$; the Gysin sequence for the associated sphere bundle identifies
$$
H^4(B\Gamma,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/|\Gamma|
$$
with generator the second Chern class of the defining two-dimensional representation. Restriction to a subgroup sends that generator to the corresponding generator and is surjective. This is also the fact recorded in [Yu, (14)].

In particular, restriction from $H^4(Q_{16},\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z/16$ to either $C_8$ or $Q_8$ is a surjection onto $\mathbb Z/8$. Both have the same kernel, the unique order-two subgroup. Vanishing on $C_8$ therefore implies vanishing on $Q_8$.

The use of a quaternion subgroup inside a binary dihedral group to eliminate an extraspecial-group cohomology class also appears in [JFT, printed p. 30]. The additional point here is the compatible lift (13) for the prescribed Barnes–Wall VOA action.

Anomaly restriction is natural and the actions agree on $Q_8$, so $\alpha|_{Q_8}=0$. Section 3 gives all cyclic involution restrictions zero. The detection lemma now gives $\alpha=0$, proving the proposed theorem. $\square$

## 6. Intended orbifold consequence and its scope

The theorem removes the anomaly hypothesis in [KRR, Conjecture 5.2]. The intended extension is the **full $E$-orbifold**, namely the sum, over conjugacy classes, of the trivial-centralizer modules after choosing an anomaly trivialization. It is not a statement that some holomorphic extension of $V_L^E$ exists if and only if the anomaly vanishes: the parent $V_L$ is always a holomorphic extension of its fixed-point algebra.

Here is the extension step explicitly. Put $W=V_L^E$. The positive definite unimodular lattice VOA $V_L$ is strongly rational and holomorphic. The finite 2-group $E$ is solvable, so [CM, Corollary 5.25] gives the regularity needed for $W$ to be strongly rational. By [GR, Theorem 3.1],
$$
\operatorname{Rep}(W)\simeq Z(\mathrm{Vec}_E^{\alpha}).
$$
All nonvacuum simple $W$-modules have positive conformal weight: the untwisted constituents occur in positive weights of $V_L$, and the nontrivial twisted sectors have ground weight at least four by the preceding standardness calculation and [KRR, §3.2]. Thus the positive ribbon structure is the one induced by the VOA, as in [GR, §§2.1–2.2]; we may transport the trivial-twist algebra below through this equivalence.

After trivializing $\alpha$, take the group algebra $\mathbb C[E]$ in $Z(\mathrm{Vec}_E)$, graded by group elements and acted on by conjugation. It is a connected, separable, braided-commutative algebra with trivial twist. Its dimension is $|E|$, so its local-module category has dimension one. Its decomposition into simple objects is
$$
\mathbb C[E]=\bigoplus_{[g]}[g,\mathbf 1_{C_E(g)}].
$$
The extension correspondence [HKL, Theorems 3.2, 3.4–3.6; GR, §2.2] therefore gives a strongly rational holomorphic VOA extension of $W$. Equivalently, it is the $K=E$, trivial-discrete-torsion case of [EG, Corollary 2 and (3.5)]. It shares the conformal vector and central charge 128. This identifies the particular full-group orbifold, rather than the parent-VOA extension corresponding to $K=1$.

The no-low-weight-state analysis in [KRR, (5.3.3)] now applies: below weight four, the extension contains only the vacuum and its Virasoro descendants. Here is an explicit witness that the gap is exactly four, without assuming a unitary extension. In orthonormal Cartesian Heisenberg coordinates $x_i=a_i(-1)$, put $P=Z_1=\operatorname{diag}(I_{64},-I_{64})$, $q=x^TPx$ and $r=x^Tx$. The state
$$
\Phi=(65q^2-r^2)\mathbf1
$$
is $E$-invariant: every Pauli generator conjugates $P$ to $\pm P$, and $r$ is orthogonally invariant. On polynomials in the $a_i(-1)$, $L_1=0$ and $L_2=\frac12\Delta$. Since $\Delta q^2=8r$ and $\Delta r^2=520r$, both $L_1\Phi$ and $L_2\Phi$ vanish. The positive Virasoro algebra is generated by $L_1,L_2$, so $\Phi$ is primary. It is nonzero because its $x_1^4$ coefficient is $64$. This makes concrete the weight-four obstruction for lattice orbifolds in [KRR, §5.1]. The full orbifold therefore has primary gap four. Section 7 establishes a unitary structure on this extension. No uniqueness claim for the VOA is made.

## 7. Unitarity of the full $E$-orbifold

We now prove a further property of the specific extension constructed in §6. Put $V=V_L$ and $W=V^E$, and let $T$ denote that full $E$-orbifold.
The anomaly trivialization and the corresponding algebra $\mathbb C[E]$ are fixed throughout. The argument proves unitarity of this algebraic VOA extension; it does not infer VOA unitarity from positive categorical dimensions.

**Proposed strengthening.** The strongly rational holomorphic VOA $T$ of §6 admits a positive invariant Hermitian form extending the natural form on $W$. Consequently the same full $E$-orbifold is unitary, with central charge 128 and primary gap four.

### 7.1 The fixed algebra is strongly unitary

The positive definite lattice VOA $V_L$ is unitary. Every prescribed element of $E$ belongs to $O(\widehat L)$ and hence preserves its Hermitian form by [Lam, Lemma 3.3]. Section 3 proves that every prescribed involution is a standard lift. Every order-four element squares to $-I$ and is fixed-point-free, so its lift is also standard. Thus all irreducible $g$-twisted $V_L$-modules, for every $g\in E$, are unitarizable by the lattice twisted-module construction of [Lam, §3.2 and Lemma 3.8], with inner-shift parameter $\beta=0$. The identity case is the ordinary lattice-module statement [Lam, Theorem 3.1]. These preliminary lattice results have no rank or central-charge-24 restriction.

The fixed algebra $W$ is already strongly rational by §6. Therefore [Gui, Proposition 10.9] applies: every irreducible $W$-module is unitarizable. In Gui's terminology, $W$ is **strongly unitary**. No claim that $W$ is completely unitary is needed below.

We use [Gui, Theorem 11.5] twice. Its hypotheses are that the base VOA is unitary, of CFT type, rational and $C_2$-cofinite, and that the given simple-current extension is **preunitarizable**, meaning unitarizable as a module over that base. It then extends the given Hermitian form to a unitary VOA structure on the same extension. The second application requires the following lemma.

### 7.2 An irreducible-restriction lemma

**Lemma.** Let $U_0=W\oplus J$ be a compatible unitary, simple, bosonic extension of a unitary strongly rational VOA $W$, with the same conformal vector and of CFT type. Suppose $J\not\cong W$ is an order-two simple current. If an ordinary $U_0$-module $M$ restricts to an irreducible unitarizable $W$-module, then every positive $W$-invariant Hermitian form on $M$ is $U_0$-invariant.

**Proof.** Fix such a form $h$, linear in its first argument. Its distinct $L_0$-eigenspaces are orthogonal. Since an ordinary module has finite-dimensional energy spaces, the antilinear map
$$
A_h:M\longrightarrow M',\qquad A_h(m)(v)=h(v,m)
$$
is a bijection onto the restricted dual. If $\Theta$ is the PCT involution of $U_0$, the transported contragredient action
$$
\widetilde Y(a,z)=A_h^{-1}Y_{M'}(\Theta a,z)A_h
\tag{14}
$$
is another ordinary $U_0$-module action. Here formal coefficients are conjugated through the antilinear maps. By $W$-invariance of $h$, this action agrees with $Y_M$ on $W$. This is the standard invariant-form identity [Lam, Lemma 2.4]; the same transported-action construction appears in [Gui, proof of Lemma 10.12, equation (10.5)].

The inequivalent unitary $W$-summands $W$ and $J$ of $U_0$ are orthogonal. Since $\Theta$ is antiunitary and preserves $W$, it preserves $J$. Choose a nonzero $\Theta$-fixed vector $j$ in the lowest-weight space of $J$, of weight $d$. The bosonic CFT-type hypotheses give $d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $L_1j=0$. Normalize the form on $U_0$ by $\|\mathbf1\|^2=1$ and write
$$
j(n)=j_{n+d-1},\qquad [L_0,j(n)]=-n\,j(n).
$$
The unitary adjoint identity on $U_0$ itself gives
$$
j_{2d-1}j=(-1)^d\|j\|^2\mathbf1.
\tag{15}
$$
Indeed, pair the left-hand side with $\mathbf1$, use
$j_{2d-1}^{\dagger}=(-1)^d j_{-1}$, and use $j_{-1}\mathbf1=j$.

On $M$, the Jacobi commutator is
$$
C_n:=[j(n),j(-n)]
=\sum_{k=0}^{2d-1}\binom{n+d-1}{k}(j_kj)_{2d-2-k}.
\tag{16}
$$
All states $j_kj$ lie in $W$, because $J\boxtimes_WJ\cong W$. Terms with $k>2d-1$ vanish by CFT-type grading. On each energy space, (16) is an operator-valued polynomial in $n$ with nonzero leading term
$$
(-1)^d\|j\|^2\binom{n+d-1}{2d-1}\operatorname{id}.
\tag{17}
$$
In particular, the $J$-action on $M$ is nonzero. Since $J$ is invertible and $M|_W$ is simple, $J\boxtimes_WM\cong M$ and the space of intertwiners of type $\binom{M}{J\ M}$ has dimension one. Consequently
$$
\widetilde Y(j,z)=\lambda Y_M(j,z)\quad(j\in J)
\tag{18}
$$
for one nonzero scalar $\lambda$. Applying (16) to the transported action multiplies its left-hand side by $\lambda^2$, while leaving its right-hand side unchanged, because the two actions agree on $W$. The nonzero leading term (17) forces $\lambda^2=1$.

Since $L_1j=0$ and $\Theta j=j$, (14) and (18) give
$$
\widetilde j(n)=(-1)^d j(-n)^\dagger,
\qquad j(-n)^\dagger=\lambda(-1)^d j(n).
$$
Fix a nonzero homogeneous $m\in M$. Ordinary modules are lower bounded, so $j(n)m=0$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $n$. Thus
$$
\begin{aligned}
\|j(-n)m\|^2
&=h\bigl(j(-n)^\dagger j(-n)m,m\bigr)\\
&=\lambda(-1)^d h(C_nm,m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
$$
By (16)–(17), the right-hand side is a polynomial with leading coefficient
$\lambda\|j\|^2\|m\|^2/(2d-1)!$.
The two signs $(-1)^d$ have canceled. A squared norm cannot be negative for all sufficiently large $n$, so $\lambda=-1$ is impossible. Hence $\lambda=1$. The two module actions now agree on $W\oplus J$, which is precisely $U_0$-invariance of $h$. $\square$

This lemma uses formal contragredience and the finite mode commutator. It requires neither complete unitarity of the base nor a conformal-net correspondence.

### 7.3 The central intermediate extension

Let $z$ be the central involution of $E$, and set $A=E/\langle z\rangle\cong C_2^{14}$. Use the equivalence $\operatorname{Rep}(W)\simeq Z(\mathrm{Vec}_E)$ of §6 with its fixed anomaly trivialization. The subalgebra
$$
D=\mathbb C[\langle z\rangle]
=\mathbf1\oplus[z,\mathbf1_E]
\subset\mathbb C[E]
$$
is connected, separable, braided-commutative and has trivial twist. Put $J=[z,\mathbf1_E]$. It is a nontrivial simple current with $J\boxtimes_WJ\cong W$. The same extension correspondence used in §6 gives an intermediate strongly rational CFT-type VOA
$$
W\subset W_1=W\oplus J\subset T.
$$
In particular, the local $D$-module category is the fusion category of ordinary $W_1$-modules [HKL, Theorems 3.4–3.6; GR, §2.2]. Its separability supplies semisimplicity; the positive-weight and finite-extension hypotheses are those already checked in §6.

By §7.1 both summands of $W_1$ are unitarizable as $W$-modules. Hence $W_1$ is a preunitarizable simple-current extension. The first application of [Gui, Theorem 11.5] makes this specific $W_1$ a unitary extension of $W$.

It remains to check the actual $W_1$-summands of $T$. Every noncentral conjugacy class of the extraspecial group $E$ is the pair $\{g,gz\}$. Consequently, as a $W$-module,
$$
T=W\oplus J\oplus\bigoplus_{0\ne a\in A}M_a,
\qquad M_a=[g,\mathbf1_{C_E(g)}]\quad(g\langle z\rangle=a).
\tag{20}
$$
Each $M_a$ is simple and has dimension two in $Z(\mathrm{Vec}_E)$. In the concrete group algebra, its underlying graded vector space is
$\operatorname{span}\{e_g,e_{gz}\}$.
Left multiplication by $e_z$ exchanges these two basis vectors. It therefore preserves $M_a$ and makes it a local $D$-module $R_a$, with underlying single irreducible $W$-module $M_a$. This module is local because it is a $D$-submodule of the braided-commutative algebra $\mathbb C[E]$. Write $R_0=D$, corresponding to the vacuum $W_1$-module.

The selected modules are simple currents. Explicitly, group multiplication induces balanced morphisms
$$
R_a\otimes_D R_b\longrightarrow R_{a+b},
\qquad e_g\otimes e_h\longmapsto e_{gh}.
\tag{21}
$$
The braiding between $D$ and these modules is the ordinary swap, since $z$ is central and conjugation acts trivially on $D$. Thus (21) is balanced in the ordinary algebraic sense and preserves both the $E$-grading and conjugation action. Each $R_a$ is free of rank one over the ordinary algebra $D$; thus the balanced tensor product has dimension two, with images $e_{gh}$ and $e_{ghz}$, so (21) is an isomorphism. In particular, $R_a\otimes_D R_a\cong D$. Equivalently, its Frobenius–Perron dimension in the local module category is $2/2=1$. There are $2^{14}=16,384$ such currents, including $R_0$.

Each $M_a$ has two inequivalent local $D$-module structures, differing by the sign of the $e_z$-action. Multiplication in the fixed algebra $\mathbb C[E]$ selects the particular $R_a$ above. Its underlying $W$-module remains irreducible.

By strong unitarity of $W$, each $M_a$ has a positive invariant Hermitian form. The lemma in §7.2, applied to the actual ordinary $W_1$-module $R_a$, makes that form $W_1$-invariant. Thus
$$
T=\bigoplus_{a\in A}R_a
$$
is preunitarizable as a $W_1$-module. It is already a simple VOA, by §6, and is a finite simple-current extension of the unitary strongly rational VOA $W_1$. A second application of [Gui, Theorem 11.5] therefore equips this same $T$ with a positive invariant Hermitian form extending the one on $W_1$, hence on $W$. This proves the proposed strengthening. $\square$

## 8. A bound on the weight-four multiplicity

Discrete torsion gives a family of full $E$-orbifolds within which one can bound the number of lightest states without determining any centralizer action explicitly.

**Proposition.** There exists a unitary strongly rational holomorphic full $E$-orbifold $T$ with inflated discrete torsion, of central charge 128 and primary gap four, such that
$$
\dim T_4\le5\,057\,652.
\tag{22}
$$
It has at most $5\,057\,650$ Virasoro primary states of weight four.

### 8.1 A global family of unitary extensions

Fix one anomaly trivialization and its orbifold-compatible equivalence
$\operatorname{Rep}(W)\simeq Z(\mathrm{Vec}_E)$, where $W=V_L^E$.
Retain $A=E/\langle z\rangle\cong\mathbb F_2^{14}$, its quadratic form $Q$, and its polar form $B_Q$. Fix an ordered basis of $A$. For each alternating bilinear form $B$ on $A$, put
$$
c_B(a,b)=\sum_{i<j}B_{ij}a_i b_j,
\qquad
\psi_B(g,h)=(-1)^{c_B(\bar g,\bar h)}.
\tag{23}
$$
Bilinearity makes $\psi_B$ a normalized two-cocycle on $E$.

Construct an algebra object $\mathcal B_B=\mathbb C_{\psi_B}[E]$ in this fixed center, with degree-$g$ basis vector $e_g$, by
$$
e_ge_h=\psi_B(g,h)e_{gh},
\qquad
x\cdot e_g
=\frac{\psi_B(x,g)}{\psi_B(xgx^{-1},x)}e_{xgx^{-1}}
=(-1)^{B(\bar g,\bar x)}e_{xgx^{-1}}.
\tag{24}
$$
The action is inner conjugation in the twisted group algebra, hence is an honest action preserving multiplication. For the center braiding
$c(e_g\otimes e_h)=g\cdot e_h\otimes e_g$, the multiplication is braided-commutative. The twist is trivial because $g\cdot e_g=e_g$. The algebra is connected and separable: a separability element is
$|E|^{-1}\sum_g e_g\otimes e_g^{-1}$, which is graded and $E$-invariant. It is simple as an algebra object because every nonzero homogeneous basis element is invertible. Its dimension is $|E|$. Thus [EG, Corollary 2 and (3.5)] and the extension correspondence of §6 give an actual holomorphic VOA $T_B$, with
$$
T_B\downarrow_W=\bigoplus_{[g]}[g,\beta_g^B],
\qquad
\beta_g^B(h)=(-1)^{B(\bar g,\bar h)}\quad(h\in C_E(g)).
\tag{25}
$$
All these objects use the same fixed identification with $\operatorname{Rep}(W)$.

The unitarity argument of §7 applies to every member of this family. Indeed,
$\psi_B(z,g)=\psi_B(g,z)=1$ and $\beta_z^B=1$, so
$D=\mathbb C[\langle z\rangle]=\mathbf1\oplus J$
and the intermediate unitary VOA $W_1=W\oplus J$ are unchanged. For each nonzero $a\in A$, the class span $R_a^B=\operatorname{span}\{e_g,e_{gz}\}$ is an actual local $D$-module whose restriction to $W$ is the single simple module $[g,\beta_g^B]$. Multiplication induces isomorphisms
$R_a^B\otimes_D R_b^B\cong R_{a+b}^B$:
both class spans are free of rank one over $D$, and the two product images form a basis of the target. Thus they are the selected simple currents over $W_1$, with $R_0^B=D$. Strong unitarity of $W$ and the irreducible-restriction lemma in §7 make them unitary $W_1$-modules. The second application of [Gui, Theorem 11.5] makes $T_B$ unitary. Every $T_B$ retains primary gap four: its nontrivial twisted sectors begin at weight at least four, and its unchanged subalgebra $W$ contains the weight-four primary of §6.

### 8.2 The counting inputs

First compute $\dim W_4$. Let $U=\mathbb C^{128}$ be the defining Heisenberg representation. The weight-four Fock pieces with invariants are $U\otimes U$, $\operatorname{Sym}^2U$, and $\operatorname{Sym}^4U$. The first two each contribute one invariant. On $\operatorname{Sym}^4U$, the two central elements have trace $\binom{131}{4}$; every noncentral element has trace $\binom{65}{2}$, whether its eigenvalues are $\pm1$ or $\pm i$, each with multiplicity 64. Therefore the Molien average gives
$$
\dim(\operatorname{Sym}^4U)^E
=\frac{2\binom{131}{4}+(32768-2)\binom{65}{2}}{32768}
=2795.
$$
The invariant Heisenberg contribution is consequently $2797$.

The other weight-four states of $V_L$ are its minimal momentum states $e^\lambda$, with $(\lambda,\lambda)=8$. By [Griess, Notation 8.7 and Proposition 8.9 in the cited author version], there are $1\,260\,230\,400$ minimal vectors and every orbit of the distinguished extraspecial subgroup $R=E$ has size $256$. Each such orbit contributes exactly one invariant even for the prescribed signed lifts. To see this, a nonidentity element fixing a nonzero lattice vector must be a noncentral involution: $z=-I$ and the order-four isometries have no fixed vectors. The standardness established in §3 makes every such stabilizer element act trivially on $e^\lambda$. Its signed orbit representation therefore has a one-dimensional invariant space. Hence
$$
\dim W_4
=2797+\frac{1\,260\,230\,400}{256}
=4\,925\,572.
\tag{26}
$$
Only the geometric lattice action is used in this orbit count.

Next consider a noncentral involution $g$. Its twisted ground weight is four. The full unprojected weight-four space has dimension $2^{16}$; a short defect calculation establishes the number. For $g=X_1$, pair the integral basis vectors as $u=w_i$, $v=w_{i+64}$ for $0\le i<64$. By [KRR, (A.2.5)],
$g(u)=-u+2^p v$, $g(v)=v$, with $p=0$ and $p=1$ on 32 pairs each. For $p=0$, the integral minus-eigenlattice in the pair is $\mathbb Z(2u-v)$, equal to the image of $1-g$. For $p=1$, it is $\mathbb Z(u-v)$, while the image is $2\mathbb Z(u-v)$. Consequently
$$
L^-/(1-g)L\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^{32},
\qquad d(g)^2=2^{32},\qquad d(g)=2^{16},
\tag{27}
$$
where the defect formula is [BK, (4.53)] for the even unimodular lattice $L$. All noncentral involutions have the same quotient by the geometric conjugacy in [KRR, Proposition 3.1]. The standard lift has zero momentum shift. In the Fock–momentum–defect decomposition [BK, Remark 4.4], every nonzero momentum and every oscillator excitation adds positive energy. Thus weight four consists exactly of the zero-momentum oscillator-vacuum fiber of dimension $2^{16}$.

The nonzero singular vectors of $(A,Q)$ index these conjugacy classes. Their number is
$2^{13}+2^6-1=8255$.
The order-four sectors begin at weight six and the central-involution sector at weight eight, so neither contributes to $T_{B,4}$.

### 8.3 Averaging the selected characters

For a fixed noncentral involution representative $g$, put $a=\bar g\ne0$ and
$C_g=C_E(g)$. Its image in $A$ is
$a^\perp=\{b:B_Q(a,b)=0\}$.
As $B$ varies, its slant character in (25) factors through
$C_g/\langle g,z\rangle\cong a^\perp/\langle a\rangle$.
The linear map
$$
\operatorname{Alt}^2(A^*)\longrightarrow
\bigl(a^\perp/\langle a\rangle\bigr)^*,
\qquad
B\longmapsto B(a,\cdot)|_{a^\perp}
\tag{28}
$$
is surjective. Indeed, extend any functional on the quotient to $\ell\in A^*$ with $\ell(a)=0$, choose $t\in A^*$ with $t(a)=1$, and take
$B(x,y)=t(x)\ell(y)+\ell(x)t(y)$.
It is alternating and has the prescribed restriction. Since the target has dimension 12, uniformly sampling the $2^{91}$ forms $B$ makes $\beta_g^B$ uniform over $2^{12}=4096$ distinct linear characters of $C_g$.

Use the centralizer linearizations associated with the single fixed anomaly trivialization. Let $\Omega_g=V_L(g)_4$ be the entire unprojected weight-four space of the $g$-twisted module, with its resulting linear $C_g$-action. The actual twisted-module decomposition [GR, Theorems 2.2 and 3.1 and the discussion following (3.1)] identifies
$$
\dim[g,\chi]_4
=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{C_g}(\chi,\Omega_g)
$$
for each linear character $\chi$. The multiplicities of distinct linear characters sum to at most $\dim\Omega_g$. If $\mathcal X_g$ denotes the 4096 characters reached in (28), this gives
$$
\mathbb E_B\,\dim[g,\beta_g^B]_4
=\frac1{4096}\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal X_g}
  \dim\operatorname{Hom}_{C_g}(\chi,\Omega_g)
\le\frac{65536}{4096}=16.
\tag{29}
$$
This inequality imposes no assumption that $g$ or $z$ acts as $+1$ on $\Omega_g$, or that its centralizer representation is trivial.

The same global $B$ is used in every class. Linearity of expectation, which requires no independence between classes, now yields
$$
\mathbb E_B\,\dim T_{B,4}
\le4\,925\,572+8255\cdot16
=5\,057\,652.
\tag{30}
$$
At least one member of the family satisfies (22). At weight four, the vacuum descendant space is spanned by $L_{-4}\mathbf1$ and $L_{-2}^2\mathbf1$. These are independent at $c=128$: their Gram determinant is $c^2(5c+22)/2>0$. Since there are no lower-weight nonvacuum primaries and $T_B$ is unitary, its weight-four primary space has dimension $\dim T_{B,4}-2$. This proves the stated bound $5\,057\,650$. $\square$

Every member contains $W$, so $4\,925\,572$ is also a lower bound for its weight-four dimension. The argument therefore bounds the minimum multiplicity in this family between $4\,925\,572$ and $5\,057\,652$. It gives an existential bound over a globally coherent family of cocycles. It specifies neither an optimizing cocycle nor the full character of the resulting VOA. The $2^{91}$ forms are a parameter family; the proof does not require them to give inequivalent theories.

## 9. The uniform Barnes–Wall family

The argument has a uniform range that is larger than the width-seven case motivating it. Here the parameter is the number of tensor factors; the lattice rank is $2^m$.

**Uniform theorem.** Let $m\ge3$ be odd, let $L_m=BW(m)$ in the exact normalization of [KRR, (A.1.1)], and let $E_m=2_+^{1+2m}$ act by the prescribed canonical generator lifts. Then its anomaly $\alpha_m$ vanishes for every odd $m\ge5$, whereas $\alpha_3\ne0$. For odd $m\ge5$, a coherent anomaly trivialization yields a unitary strongly rational holomorphic full $E_m$-orbifold $T_m$ of central charge $n=2^m$. Its primary gap is exactly four for odd $m\ge7$. For odd $m\ge9$,
$$
\dim(T_m)_4=\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}6+2,
\qquad P_4(T_m):=\dim\operatorname{Prim}_4(T_m)
=\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}6.
\tag{31}
$$
These counts also hold after any inflated discrete-torsion choice constructed as in §8. No gap-four assertion is made at $m=5$, and no uniqueness of these VOAs is asserted.

### 9.1 The parameter dependence of the anomaly proof

The cohomological input [JFT, §3.3] is valid for $m\ge3$. With
$r_m=\binom{2m}{2}+\binom{2m}{3}$, it gives
$$
H^4(E_m,\mathbb Z)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^{r_m-1}\oplus\mathbb Z/4,
\qquad \operatorname{im}\pi^*=H^4(E_m,\mathbb Z)[2].
\tag{32}
$$
The inflation kernel is again the span of $\beta(\ell Q)$ for linear $\ell$. The anisotropic $Q_8$ calculation of §2 detects the unique nonzero divisible-by-two class. The Boolean cubic argument uses only three distinct coordinate indices. Thus the detection lemma holds throughout this range.

Standardness is uniform for odd $m\ge5$. In §3 replace the six-dimensional exterior space by the space on $e_2,\ldots,e_m$, of dimension $d=m-1$. The half-Gram decomposition in [KRR, Lemmas A.1, A.3–A.4] gives the same first-factor phases $q_{X_1}=\mathfrak q(x)$ and $q_{Z_1}=\mathfrak q(y)$, with the other generator phases zero. The $H_2$ contribution vanishes because the binary generator increments take $V_0$ into $V_1$ and kill $V_1$; one must not assume that the entire half-Gram matrix interchanges parity. The identity $\mathfrak q(Cu)=Q_0\mathfrak q(u)$ follows exactly as in (8): two one-bit neighbors cannot be complementary when $d>2$. The fixed-vector equations then prove standardness for every prescribed involution, including at $m=5$.

For the compatible quaternion lift, write $m=2k+1$ and $p_i=(m-|i|)\bmod2$. Directly from the ordered lattice basis,
$$
G_{ij}=2^{k-d(i,j)/2+(p_i+p_j)/2},
\qquad H_{ii}=2^{k-1+p_i},
\tag{33}
$$
where $d(i,j)$ is Hamming distance and $H$ is the half-Gram matrix of §4. In a block obtained by fixing bits $4,\ldots,m$, the off-diagonal Gram entries have valuation at least $k-1$. The diagonal entries of $H$ are also even for $k\ge2$. Hence every such eight-coordinate block has $H|_{\mathrm{block}}=0$ modulo two. At $m=5$ the diagonal entries are $2$ or $4$; divisibility by four is unnecessary.

Keep $a=Y_1$, $b=Z_1Y_2$ and $g=(I+Y_1)(X_3+Z_3)/2$. In the width-$m$ basis its rows are
$$
w_i g=\begin{cases}
2^{p_i}w_{i^{\{3\}}}-w_{i^{\{1,3\}}},&i_1=0,\\
w_{i^{\{1,3\}}},&i_1=1.
\end{cases}
\tag{34}
$$
Thus $g$ and its inverse $g^7$ are integral. The tensor identities of §4 still give $\langle g,b\rangle\cong Q_{16}$. All the relevant generators preserve these blocks, so the block-cocycle lemma gives their exact lift relations and agreement with the prescribed common $Q_8$. There is no character correction or full-normalizer lifting assumption.

The standard-lift ground weights and cyclic-type tests are:

| Element | Actual order $N$ | Ground weight $\rho$ | $N\rho$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $z$ | $2$ | $n/16$ | $2^{m-3}$ |
| Noncentral involution | $2$ | $n/32$ | $2^{m-4}$ |
| Order-four element of $E_m$ | $4$ | $3n/64$ | $3\cdot2^{m-4}$ |
| $g$ | $8$ | $11n/256$ | $11\cdot2^{m-5}$ |

The first three rows use [KRR, Proposition 3.1 and §3.2]; order-four elements square to $-I$ and are fixed-point-free. For $g$, each primitive eighth root has multiplicity $n/4$. Every displayed $N\rho$ is integral when $m\ge5$, so the corresponding type $N^2\rho\bmod N$ is zero. The common restriction kernel from $Q_{16}$ to $C_8$ and $Q_8$, followed by the detection lemma, proves $\alpha_m=0$.

At $m=3$, [KRR, Proposition 3.4 and Theorem 3.5] still supplies the prescribed order-preserving action. An order-four element is fixed-point-free and has $\rho=3/8$. Its cyclic type is $16\rho=6\equiv2\pmod4$, so $\alpha_3\ne0$. This is an actual obstruction, making five the sharp lower boundary among the odd parameters under consideration.

### 9.2 Existence and unitarity in the uniform range

For odd $m\ge5$, $L_m$ is positive definite, even and unimodular. The fixed algebra $W_m=V_{L_m}^{E_m}$ is strongly rational by [CM, Corollary 5.25]. Every nontrivial twisted sector starts at weight at least $2^{m-5}\ge1$; every nonvacuum untwisted constituent also has positive weight. Hence the positivity and ribbon hypotheses in §6 apply. After a coherent anomaly trivialization, the actual algebra $\mathbb C[E_m]$ gives the strongly rational holomorphic full-group extension by [GR, HKL, EG].

The unitarity proof in §7 has no additional rank restriction. Lam's lattice statements and [Gui, Proposition 10.9] make $W_m$ strongly unitary. The central constituent $J_m=[z,\mathbf1]$ has order two and positive integral weight, at least $n/16\ge2$. The first application of [Gui, Theorem 11.5] makes $W_m\oplus J_m$ unitary. Each noncentral conjugacy class is still $\{g,gz\}$, so its selected module restricts irreducibly to $W_m$ and the explicit lemma of §7.2 applies unchanged. The actual multiplication gives the $2^{2m}$ selected simple currents over the intermediate extension. The second application of Gui's theorem makes $T_m$ unitary. The same argument applies to formula (23) with $A$ replaced by $\mathbb F_2^{2m}$; these inflated cocycles have trivial restrictions involving $z$.

### 9.3 The gap and exact weight-four spectrum

For odd $m\ge7$, nonzero lattice momenta start at weight $2^{(m-3)/2}\ge4$, and all nontrivial twisted sectors start at $2^{m-5}\ge4$. Below four, only the invariant zero-momentum Heisenberg space contributes; its dimensions at weights one, two and three are $0,1,1$. The latter two states are vacuum descendants. The explicit primary of §6 generalizes to
$$
\Phi_m=\left(\frac{n+2}{2}q^2-r^2\right)\mathbf1,
\qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(I_{n/2},-I_{n/2}),
$$
with $q=x^TPx$ and $r=x^Tx$. Here $\Delta q^2=8r$ and $\Delta r^2=4(n+2)r$, so it is primary; its $x_1^4$ coefficient is $n/2\ne0$. Thus the gap is exactly four.

For odd $m\ge9$, the momentum and nontrivial twisted thresholds are at least eight and sixteen, respectively. Only the invariant Heisenberg space $F^{E_m}$ contributes at weight four. The character average in §8.2 becomes
$$
M=\dim(\operatorname{Sym}^4\mathbb C^n)^{E_m}
=\frac{2\binom{n+3}{4}+(2n^2-2)\binom{n/2+1}{2}}{2n^2}
=\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}6.
\tag{35}
$$
The two other invariant oscillator partitions give $\dim F_4^{E_m}=M+2$. To count primaries directly, the map $(L_1,L_2)$ on $L_{-4}\mathbf1,L_{-2}^2\mathbf1$, in the target bases $L_{-3}\mathbf1,L_{-2}\mathbf1$, has matrix
$$
\begin{pmatrix}5&3\\6&n+8\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det=5n+22>0.
$$
The target has dimension two, and the kernel is precisely the primary subspace. This proves (31) independently of a Virasoro semisimplicity assumption. The absence of twisted states at weight four also makes the count independent of the inflated discrete-torsion choice.

### 9.4 Distinction from iterated swap orbifolds

Write $P_4(V)$ for the dimension of the weight-four Virasoro-primary space. Fix once and for all a sparse full $E(7)$ orbifold $T_0$ supplied by §8, and put $P_0=P_4(T_0)$. Then
$$
4\,925\,570\le P_0\le5\,057\,650.
$$
The lower bound comes from the common fixed-point subalgebra $V_{BW(7)}^{E(7)}$ of these full $E(7)$ orbifolds; it is not asserted for arbitrary central-charge-128 seeds.

Let $S(V)$ be the type-zero swap orbifold of $V\otimes V$. At a stage with $c(V)=c_j=128\cdot2^j$, [BDM, proof of Theorem 3.9, printed p. 23] gives
$$
L_0^\sigma=\tfrac12L_0+\frac{c_j}{16},
\qquad \rho_\sigma=8\cdot2^j,
\qquad 4\rho_\sigma\equiv0\pmod2.
$$
The nontrivial untwisted eigenspace contains no vacuum, and both twisted constituents have positive ground weight. Thus [vEMS, Theorem 5.16 and its type-zero specialization] supplies a strongly rational holomorphic extension. Its twisted summand contributes nothing through weight four. The swap preserves the dimensions $0,1,1$ at weights one, two, and three; at weight four, the untwisted invariants gain exactly the one-dimensional $V_2\otimes V_2$ contribution. Subtracting the two vacuum descendants therefore gives
$$
P_4(S(V))=P_4(V)+1.
$$
Thus swaps preserve primary gap four, and $P_4(S^r(T_0))=P_0+r$. The comparison uses these algebraic properties of the swap extensions.

For odd $m\ge9$, the direct orbifold $T_m$ has $D_m=P_4(T_m)=(2^m+1)(2^m+2)/6$. Matching central charges requires $r=m-7$:

| $m$ | $D_m$ | Bounds for $P_4(S^{m-7}(T_0))$ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| $9$ | $43\,947$ | $[4\,925\,572,\ 5\,057\,652]$ |
| $11$ | $700\,075$ | $[4\,925\,574,\ 5\,057\,654]$ |
| $13$ | $11\,188\,907$ | $[4\,925\,576,\ 5\,057\,656]$ |

The first two rows separate using the seed lower bound; the third uses its upper bound. For $n=2^m$,
$$
D_{m+2}-D_m=\frac{5n^2+3n}{2}>2,
$$
whereas the swap count increases by two. The strict separation at $m=13$ therefore persists. Consequently, for every odd $m\ge9$, $T_m$ and $S^{m-7}(T_0)$ are nonisomorphic as conformal VOAs. The same fixed seed works throughout.

This distinguishes the direct family from the stated sequence of swap orbifolds; it does not establish novelty against all previously known VOAs. Higher-central-charge existence alone already follows from a gap-four seed by this permutation construction. The uniform contribution is the anomaly calculation for the prescribed action, its sharp odd-parameter threshold, and the direct construction with its exact low-weight count.
